items.title: Three-dimensional mapping of intact ovaries reveals the aging dynamics of the ovarian reserve
items.author: Elvan Böke
items.content: The spatiotemporal dynamics of the depletion of the ovarian reserve remain incompletely understood. Combining whole-ovary imaging, AI and modeling, the authors mapped over 85,000 mouse oocytes and found that ovaries maintain a stable fraction of newly activated oocytes throughout aging, suggesting organ-wide control of oocyte activation.

items.title: TNFR1 signaling connects inflammation to impaired fatty acid oxidation to drive intestinal stem cell aging
items.author: Derek M. Huffman
items.content: Wang et al. identify TNFR1 signaling as a key link between inflammation and intestinal stem cell aging. This aging phenotype is transferable from old to young mice via shared circulation, suggesting systemic inflammation as a target to improve intestinal health.

items.title: Maladaptive trained immunity as a hematopoietic stem cell driver of inflammaging
items.author: Katherine Y. King
items.content: A new study reveals that aging hematopoietic stem cells trigger a form of innate immune memory, known as trained immunity, that fuels the chronic low-grade inflammation that underlies age-related physiological decline. SIRT3, a mitochondrial deacetylase whose expression wanes with age, emerges as a key molecular brake on this process.

items.title: Ultra-early proteomic signatures predict MASLD up to 16 years ahead
items.content: A plasma proteomic signature enables accurate prediction of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) up to 16 years before diagnosis, and offers a clinically applicable proteomic framework for early risk stratification and preventive intervention.
